attribution_limitations: The clinic presentation is placed in the third month after the COVID-19 hospitalization, while the C. difficile diarrhea and the Day-28 events are dated from discharge after 14 days; the source does not reconcile these time frames.

The text first reports bacterial cultures positive for Klebsiella pneumoniae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa without a date and later fungal cultures, while Table A2 places isolates at Day-28 and at the second, third and fourth month. The source does not state which text culture corresponds to which table time point, so both are kept.

The sentence describing the Day-28 event is garbled (left hemiparesis, an explosion of the left eyeball and unilateral visual loss with missing verbs), so the exact symptoms that appeared are read literally.
The MRI sentence says the left eyeball was exophthalmic on the right side and describes infiltration of the internal right eye muscle; the side is internally inconsistent in the source.

The stroke is an ambulatory diagnosis made before brain imaging; the head MRI describing an ischemic-character left cortical image is undated and the Figure 2 caption calls it a left sided cerebrovascular accident on the 28th day after COVID-19 diagnosis.

Table A1 prints units only for some rows (lymphocytes, neutrophils, N/Ly, INR carry none) and the column group headers COVID-Hospitalization and Infectious Diseases Daily Clinic Follow-Up lose their column spans in the text; lymphocyte and neutrophil values are printed as counts while their normal ranges are printed with x 10^(3).
Piperacillin/Tazobactam is listed in the description of the treatment strategy without a start date or an explicit administration statement; it is recorded as administered for 21 days as written.
Oxygen supplementation is said to have been required for two months post-COVID-19; whether it was administered continuously is not stated.
